📖 The Codex turns a page on its own. Lockpick is dead. You didn't ask. It knew.

⚔️ Jesse killed the Lockpick with their party — 1 round, 2 taken. Word travels fast. Cornered at the treeline, it could not slip away before a blow. The carcass is out there — haul it home before it rots.

The treeline is quiet. No shapes in the dark.
The door is quiet. Haven breathes.
🛟 Quinn stands up by the fire. "We take the hit and we answer it — standing here isn't an answer. Here's what we CAN do — pick one, maybe two, but everything costs something."
"There's hurt to tend and bellies to fill. Triage for the hurt, rations to stretch what's left, or a hard hunt to replace what we lost."
"Or we rally," Quinn adds. "Second shift, everybody. We work, we eat, we live — and we pay for it."
(Relief is open — triage, rations, hunt, or rally, from the beats row. Each option works once; the moment passes in ~3 days.)

sayLines.line: Filled 1L (clean — Haven well). 3L carried (3kg). (-10 kcal hauling, 1 tick.) Cistern: 24L left.
A woman, maybe 20s shakes their head. "Ask someone who trusts you." (Trust too low.)

Travel 1 tile to creek.
— Moving water —
Something big drank here recently — the mud is churned to soup on the far bank. You drink from the near side, upstream of whatever it was.
Unfamiliar unknown nuts — into the bag. (Unknowns lump together; sort them at camp.)
Journal: Slow water. The cattails stand thick.
The System notes the synergy — foraged a plant new to this ground: +1 field XP.
📓 Journal: you UNDERSTAND Green Thumb, Literally. It resonates with: something unnamed, something unnamed.
A shot in the dark — you take what's green: 5× unknown nuts. Into the bag, unnamed. (Not food until identified — sort them at camp.) This patch is picked clean — it'll recover in a few days.

Travel 2 tiles to creek.
— Moving water —
A kingfisher works the far bank, patient as a tax collector. It catches something silver and is gone before you can envy it properly.
You see smoke on the horizon. Emberhold — 10 people, 1 day in. fishing folk, by the look of it. They know 4 plants — 4 new to you. They've been here the whole time.
This patch is worked out — step to another green patch and forage again.

Travel 2 tiles to forest floor.
— Under the canopy —
Fallen trunks lie like sleeping animals, furred with moss. The ground gives underfoot — centuries of leaf-mold.
Unfamiliar unknown nuts — into the bag. (Unknowns lump together; sort them at camp.)
Journal: Deep shade. The floor keeps its secrets.
A shot in the dark — you take what's green: 4× unknown nuts. Into the bag, unnamed. (Not food until identified — sort them at camp.) This patch is picked clean — it'll recover in a few days.
📖 LEARNED: Old World Caches (Level 1). You know where people hid things: under floorboards, in hollow trees, behind loose bricks.
You've learned Old World Caches — it carries Eagle Eye.

Travel 2 tiles to grove.
— Nut trees —
Bark stripped at deer height on a young hickory — teeth, winter, hunger. Somebody winters here. Maybe you will too.
Some of these unknown nuts are starting to look familiar — sort them at camp in good light and the name might come to you.
Journal: Riparian ground. Water means life, and lunch.
A shot in the dark — you take what's green: 4× unknown nuts. Into the bag, unnamed. (Not food until identified — sort them at camp.) This patch is picked clean — it'll recover in a few days.
Travel 1 tile to Haven.
You keep a day's food (1400 kcal) — nothing extra for the pantry this time.
1 unprocessed haul onto the counter — the clock is ticking.
Someone by the fire nods at the counter. "We pool food here. Keep what you need for the road — the rest feeds everyone, once it's food."
Nobody at the fire knows your haul any better than you do. It'll be your own hands that teach you.
You walk back into Haven. 2 Codex entries. The village is glad to see you.
A woman, maybe 20s heads out to forage. "Bringing dinner back. One way or another." Good kit is the difference out there.
A person, maybe 50s, with deep-set eyes walks away from Haven. They don't look back.
A man, maybe 60s, with a shaved head heads out for water. "Water first. Everything else waits." The pantry won't fill itself.
A person, maybe 50s, with tattooed arms heads out for water. "Off to the well — back with a full skin." The pantry won't fill itself.
A man, maybe 40s heads out for water. "Thirst doesn't negotiate. Going." The pantry won't fill itself.
A woman, maybe 30s, with a crooked nose heads out for water. "The well won't fill itself." The pantry won't fill itself.
A man, maybe 60s, with calloused knuckles heads out for water. "Thirst doesn't negotiate. Going." The pantry won't fill itself.
A man, maybe 50s, with a missing fingertip walks away from Haven. They don't look back.
A man, maybe 50s, with a broad frame sets out to find A woman, maybe 20s. "Won't be long." Company makes the road shorter.
A woman, maybe 30s, with a wiry build heads out for water. "Off to the well — back with a full skin." The pantry won't fill itself.
Iron cold. Even the ticks are shelved.
— MIDDAY — Honest work hours. Heat builds.
You wait. The light changes. Nothing asks anything of you.
You eat Dried meat (600 kcal).
"You haven't earned that yet," A woman, maybe 20s says. (Trust too low.)
📋 A man, maybe 50s, with a missing fingertip wants to know what's by the creek. "Just look. Come back and tell me."
— DUSK — Animals stir again. Shadows lengthen.
You wait. The light changes. Nothing asks anything of you.
A woman, maybe 20s shakes their head. "Ask someone who trusts you." (Trust too low.)
🌿 A woman, maybe 20s returns from foraging the wilds: +214 kcal to the pantry.
💧 A man, maybe 60s, with a shaved head returns with water: +3 clean.
Recipe: Bark armor (Level 1). You have seen bark armor. Plates of bark laced together, worn like a shell.

🛡️ A man, maybe 60s, with a shaved head catches you eyeing the bark plates — claw-scored, vine-laced. "...Want to actually SEE one?" They talk you through it — wide strips dried flat, laced overlapping like shingles, snug but not tight. Your hands don't know it yet. Your eyes do.
💧 A person, maybe 50s, with tattooed arms returns with water: +2 clean.

Night. The treeline is just a sound now. The fire is the whole argument against it.
You wait. The light changes. Nothing asks anything of you.

💧 A man, maybe 40s returns with water: +4 clean.

"Hey." A man, maybe 50s, with a missing fingertip settles near you, not too close. "Day one. Everyone's pretending they're fine. ...Can we talk? Just talk — like people used to." (Talk to A man, maybe 50s, with a missing fingertip.)
⚠ STARVING: health and energy falling. You went to bed on an empty stomach.
Village meal: +1014 kcal, +1L water from the communal pantry. (Half ration — they don't trust you yet.)
A man, maybe 60s, with calloused knuckles is staring into the fire like it owes them answers.

A man, maybe 40s spends the afternoon with the tree with lobed leaves and oval nuts in scaly caps — look, smell, the smallest taste, then waiting. Raw, it knots the stomach. Cooked... fine. The fire learns the rule before the name: cook it, or else.
From the lumped bag: White Oak Acorns — named, and out.
★ IDENTIFIED: White Oak Acorns. White oak acorn. Lobed leaves, sweet acorns. Uses unknown — harvest, taste, and learn.
💡 You see it again in your mind: a tree with lobed leaves and oval nuts in scaly caps. A man, maybe 40s's words land on the memory like a label. White Oak Acorns. Of course.
The Journal notes it: White Oak Acorns — cook it, or else. (A man, maybe 40s tested it.)
A man, maybe 50s, with a missing fingertip traded something with someone for something else. The barter economy stirs.
🔍 A crouches over a tree with compound leaves and hard nuts, studying it a moment before moving on. (1/3 looks)
A woman, maybe 30s, with a crooked nose came back with 450 kcal of something edible. The pantry breathes.
Michael and Nancy lingered over the fire together.
You remember the Sharpened stick at your space in the haven and fetch it — it rides in your pack now.
You remember the Rain poncho at your space in the haven and fetch it — it rides in your pack now.
📓 Journal: the man in his 60s, with a shaved head taught the man in his 40s Soft Step.

The fire burns low. One new line in the journal: White Oak Acorns — named and noted.
👀 Someone asks the woman in her 30s, with a crooked nose, the wild food forager a shop-talk question about Wild food forager work. The pause before the answer is long enough to hear.
📓 Journal: jotted down what they said (A woman, maybe 30s, with a crooked nose).
Theo Medina reads the sky: clear tomorrow, cold.
Hunger gnaws. The pack is thin — work the green, haul it back, get it named at camp. That's the whole game.
A man, maybe 40s will work the garden once each day while at Haven. Other orders take priority.
